nodes.label: Derived from Working Code Not Aspiration
nodes.rationale: Only principles the implemented architecture actually demonstrates are listed; a principle that sounded reasonable but the real implementation does not enforce is excluded.

nodes.label: Principle 1: Engineering Entities Have Stable Identities
nodes.rationale: Id and Kind never change after creation; no method accepts a new Id for an existing document.

nodes.label: Principle 2: Revision History Is Explicit
nodes.rationale: Every content change is a new separately retrievable revision; there is no update in place.

nodes.label: Principle 3: Engineering Data Is Independent of Calculations
nodes.rationale: Content is an opaque string; the namespace contains no formula or numeric computation.

nodes.label: Principle 4: Engineering Entities Are Immutable Where Practical
nodes.rationale: A revision once written is never modified; CurrentRevisionNumber advancing is the one narrow structural exception.

nodes.label: Principle 5: Engineering Information Is Reproducible
nodes.rationale: Reading the same Id and revision always returns the same content, a consequence of principles 2 and 4.

nodes.label: Principle 6: Engineering Correctness Takes Precedence over Convenience
nodes.rationale: ReviseAsync serialises concurrent revisions with a per-document lock because a colliding revision number is worse than a slower write.

nodes.label: Principle 7: Units Are Explicit
nodes.rationale: A bare double never represents a physical quantity; the Quantity constructor requires both value and unit.

nodes.label: Principle 8: Dimensions Are Enforced
nodes.rationale: The compiler rejects adding Length to Mass; CompileTimeDimensionSafetyTests documents the exact CS1503/CS0019 errors.

nodes.label: Principle 9: Conversion Is Deterministic
nodes.rationale: Pure multiplication against a fixed factor; formatting and parsing hard-coded to InvariantCulture.

nodes.label: Principle 10: Physical Impossibilities Fail Loudly
nodes.rationale: Zero, negative, infinite or NaN factors and values are rejected in the constructor, never clamped.

nodes.label: Principle 11: Precision Loss Is Never Silent
nodes.rationale: Default ToString is full round-trippable; division by zero throws rather than producing Infinity.

nodes.label: Principle 12: Mathematical Correctness Takes Precedence over Convenience
nodes.rationale: Operators require the exact same Unit, throwing IncompatibleUnitsException; implicit conversion the caller did not ask for is a correctness risk (ADR-0054 Decision 4).

nodes.label: Principle 13: Every Engineering Property Has Provenance
nodes.rationale: MaterialProperty cannot be constructed without a provenance; Unknown is a real present value, never an omitted field.

nodes.label: Principle 14: Engineering Data Is Revision Controlled
nodes.rationale: Material properties are never updated in place; ReviseAsync records a new document revision.

nodes.label: Principle 15: Engineering Values Remain Independent of Design Methodology
nodes.rationale: No safety factor, design allowable or design-code assumption; a property value is the fact as sourced.

nodes.label: Principle 16: Material Identity Is Stable
nodes.rationale: MaterialId, Name and Category never change once registered.

nodes.label: Principle 17: Every Calculation Is Reproducible
nodes.rationale: Calculate is a pure function of its input; the same input five times gives the identical result.

nodes.label: Principle 18: Every Assumption Is Explicit
nodes.rationale: CalculationMetadata.Assumptions is copied into every record; no code path produces a record without them.

nodes.label: Principle 19: Every Engineering Input Is Traceable
nodes.rationale: A record Id is the real durable IEngineeringDocument Id backing it.

nodes.label: Principle 20: Every Engineering Output Records Provenance
nodes.rationale: The record itself is the provenance: CalculationId, ExecutedAt, ExecutedByPrincipalId, Assumptions, ReferencedMaterialIds.

nodes.label: Principle 21: Intermediate Results Are Inspectable
nodes.rationale: CalculationContext.RecordIntermediate discloses named values computed on the way to the result.

nodes.label: Principle 22: Calculations Remain Deterministic
nodes.rationale: Thirty concurrent executions with different inputs produce exactly the result each input implies, with no cross-contamination.

nodes.label: Principle 23: Engineering Judgement Is Never Hidden Inside Algorithms
nodes.rationale: The framework supplies dispatch, metadata, context and recording only, mirroring ICommandRegistry supplying no command logic.

nodes.label: Principle 24: Every Engineering Conclusion Is Independently Verifiable
nodes.rationale: RecordAsync requires a real subject, an explicit outcome and a named method, durably recorded as its own document.

nodes.label: Principle 25: Verification Evidence Is Explicit
nodes.rationale: RecordCriterion and RecordEvidence disclose what was checked and what supports the outcome.

nodes.label: Principle 26: Verification Is Repeatable
nodes.rationale: Multiple verifications against the same subject are independent records, never overwriting.

nodes.label: Principle 27: Engineering Conclusions Remain Traceable
nodes.rationale: Every linked document and calculation record is validated at recording time, not stored as an unverified string.

nodes.label: Principle 28: Verification Is Independent of Presentation
nodes.rationale: No report formatting, UI concern or approval-workflow logic; presentation is a different framework.

nodes.label: Principle 29: Requirement Lifecycle Status Is Independent of Verification Outcome
nodes.rationale: RequirementStatus is never derived from a VerificationRecord outcome; no code path connects RecordAsync to SetStatusAsync.

nodes.label: Principle 30: Engineering Workflow Is a Closed Contractual State Model
nodes.rationale: A single fixed exhaustively-tested transition table decides every transition; the first principle constraining a sequence of facts.

nodes.label: Principle 31: Traceability and Allocation Targets Are Kind-Agnostic
nodes.rationale: LinkAsync validates a target for existence only, never for Kind; discipline-neutral as a structural guarantee.

nodes.label: Principle 32: A Digital Thread Requires Only Composed Reads
nodes.rationale: GetEvidenceAsync composes existing permission-gated reads with no new storage, index or query mechanism.

nodes.label: Principle 33: A Calculation Is Complete Only with Its Reference Diagram
nodes.rationale: Product Owner rule 2026-10-01 (PO-2, ADR-0158): every calculation has exactly one CalculationDiagramSpec and EveryCalculation_HasExactlyOneReferenceDiagram fails the build otherwise; a form an engineer cannot picture is a form filled in wrongly.
